params.body:
Step 2 of the open point `2fa-en-passkeys` (step 1, long sessions, landed in #548). Decision `tweede-factor-opt-in` (Shane, 18 September 2026). Everything sits behind the feature flag **`two_factor`** (Beheer > Functies, stages off / admins / dealers / everyone), so it releases per stage; with the flag off the login is exactly what it was.

## What changed for the user

- **Mijn profiel** (`settings/profile`, menu link "Beveiliging" under the user name while the flag is on, for every user whatever their role): account details and a **Beveiliging** section. Enable an authenticator app (QR + key, confirm with a code, recovery codes shown once, "Nieuwe herstelcodes", disable), **passkeys** (list with name / created / last used / delete, "Passkey toevoegen"), and **"Meld alle andere toestellen af"**. Every change asks the password first (the section shows the password form until confirmed, `auth.password_timeout`).
- **Login**: a user with a confirmed factor goes to `/two-factor-challenge` (code or recovery code, `?recovery=1`) instead of straight in; a valid code logs in with the same session setup as before (rights, remember flag) and sets the **`sl_device`** cookie (90 days, HMAC per user) so this browser is not asked again. "Meld alle andere toestellen af" rotates that secret, rotates `remember_token`, deletes the user's other rows in `sessions`, and re-issues both for the browser that pressed the button.
- **"Aanmelden met passkey"** on the login page (visible when the flag is not `off`; who may come in is decided per user on the server): logs in without password or code, with the gates of the password login (active, demo database matches the dealer, flag on for the user). Passkey autofill on the email field (`autocomplete="username webauthn"`).
- Delegation ("werken als") never asks a second factor and sets no device cookie.

## Fortify wiring and the route diff

`laravel/fortify ^1.39` (bundles `laravel/passkeys` 0.2), `fortify:install` run, then stripped: the unused action stubs were removed, config keeps only `Features::twoFactorAuthentication(['confirm' => true, 'confirmPassword' => true])` and `Features::passkeys(['confirmPassword' => true])`, `views => false`, provider registered in `config/app.php`.

**Choice: `Fortify::ignoreRoutes()` and our own subset in `routes/_partials/Auth.php`.** Fortify's `routes/routes.php` registers unconditionally `GET /login` (name `login`), `POST /login` (`login.store`) and `POST /logout` (`logout`), plus `password.confirm`/`password.confirmation`. Ours live at the same paths and names (`LoginController`, `routes/web.php`); Laravel keeps the last route per name and the last registered per path, so letting Fortify register would have silently replaced the dealer login with Fortify's (its username field, its limiter, none of the demo-database logic of R P2-3.1) and turned our `GET /logout` into a `POST`. With `ignoreRoutes()` the route list before and after differs by exactly these 16 routes, all behind `feature:two_factor` (404 while off) and all with Fortify's paths and names so its redirects and the `@laravel/passkeys` client find them:

```
+ GET|HEAD  two-factor-challenge                    two-factor.login                      guest, feature:two_factor
+ POST      two-factor-challenge                    two-factor.login.store                guest, feature, throttle:two-factor
+ GET|HEAD  passkeys/login/options                  passkey.login-options                 guest, feature, throttle:passkeys
+ POST      passkeys/login                          passkey.login                         guest, feature, throttle:passkeys
+ GET|HEAD  settings/profile                        profile.show                          auth, feature
+ GET|HEAD  user/confirm-password                   password.confirm                      auth, feature  (redirects to the profile)
+ POST      user/confirm-password                   password.confirm.store                auth, feature
+ POST      user/two-factor-authentication          two-factor.enable                     auth, feature, password.confirm
+ POST      user/confirmed-two-factor-authentication two-factor.confirm                   auth, feature, password.confirm
+ DELETE    user/two-factor-authentication          two-factor.disable                    auth, feature, password.confirm
+ POST      user/two-factor-recovery-codes          two-factor.regenerate-recovery-codes  auth, feature, password.confirm
+ GET|HEAD  user/passkeys/options                   passkey.registration-options          auth, feature, password.confirm, throttle
+ POST      user/passkeys                           passkey.store                         auth, feature, password.confirm, throttle
+ DELETE    user/passkeys/{passkey}                 passkey.destroy                       auth, feature, password.confirm
+ POST      settings/profile/forget-devices         profile.forget-devices                auth, feature, password.confirm
```
No existing route changed. Not registered on purpose: Fortify's JSON routes for QR / secret / recovery codes (rendered server-side), the passkey-as-password-confirmation routes, and everything of registration, password reset, email verification and profile update.

Other pieces: `App\Support\TwoFactor` (does this login ask a code; may this passkey come in), `App\Support\RememberedDevice` (the cookie), `App\Http\Middleware\RequireFeature` (`feature:<key>`), `App\Http\Responses\{TwoFactorLoginResponse,PasskeyLoginResponse}` (run `LoginController::authenticated()`, set the device cookie), `App\Http\Controllers\Settings\ProfileController`. User model: `TwoFactorAuthenticatable`, `PasskeyAuthenticatable`, implements `PasskeyUser`; the three secrets are `$hidden`. Migrations dated today: Fortify's three columns plus `two_factor_device_secret`, and `passkeys` (with `user_id` as unsigned INT: `users.id` is `int(10) unsigned`, the package's `foreignIdFor` BIGINT would not take the FK). Browser side: new Vite entry `resources/js/passkeys.js` with `@laravel/passkeys` 0.4 (npm, no CDN), loaded only on the login and the profile; guest layout gained a csrf meta and a `scripts` stack.

## Rules, docs, tests

- R P2-3.12 to P2-3.19 in `32-p2-mijn-garage.md`; decision `bronnen/beslissingen/2026-09-18-tweede-factor-opt-in.md`; open point updated (steps 1 and 2 done, step 3 email code open, admin requirement a separate decision). `php bin/rules-sources`: "Geen problemen".
- `docs/auth.md`: operator notes (relying party id = host of `APP_URL`, `PASSKEYS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` / `PASSKEYS_RELYING_PARTY_ID` optional env keys, preview needs its own origin or a shared RP id, localhost vs 127.0.0.1, rate limiters, what to do for a locked-out user).
- Flag: `two_factor` in `Features::catalogue()` and `features.php` in nl/fr/en/de; copy in `resources/lang/{nl,fr,en,de}/security.php`; Fortify's three English messages translated in `nl.json`.
- Tests: `TwoFactorTest` (15) and `PasskeyRoutesTest` (5): flag off = 404 everywhere, no menu link, no button, login unchanged even with a confirmed factor; enable + QR + confirm ok/wrong; recovery codes shown once then count; disable; challenge ok / wrong / no challenged user; recovery code works once; remembered device skips the challenge, another user's or a tampered cookie does not; forget-devices rotates and keeps this browser in; password confirmation gate; passkey guest options carry the RP id; registration needs login (401) and a fresh password (423); a passkey can only be deleted by its owner; passkey login gates; delegation asks nothing.

Hot shared files: none of the listed ones (`navigation.blade.php` got the menu link, not `app.blade.php`; `refresh.css`/`ui.php` untouched, all styling is Tailwind utilities plus existing `ui-` classes).

## Not in this PR (open)

- Step 3, the email code as second factor; making the factor mandatory for administrators (separate decision).
- Recovering a user who lost phone and recovery codes: today a manual NULL on the three columns (docs/auth.md); a button for administrators is a follow-up.
- A WebAuthn ceremony end to end was not exercised (needs a real authenticator); the routes, options payload and guards are tested, the browser client is Laravel's own.
params.title: Second factor (TOTP + recovery codes) and passkeys through Fortify, behind the two_factor flag
